sections.html:
Topeka is the Kansas capital and the seat of Shawnee County. The 2020 count was 126,587 residents. The city grew around the Kansas River, and much of the housing near downtown dates from the decades after the 1854 layout and the railroad shops that opened in 1878. An older house can come with old wiring, plumbing or a foundation question, so describe its real condition and location to buyers instead of a generic one.

The county handles values, tax bills and deeds. The city handles code enforcement and permits. Knowing which office does what saves you phone calls.

sections.h2: Property maintenance rules and code notices
sections.html:
Topeka enforces the International Property Maintenance Code through its Property Maintenance Unit, and an unresolved violation stays with the property when it changes hands. The unit works from 620 SE Madison and takes complaints by phone at 785-368-3161, by email or through SeeClickFix.

A code official schedules an inspection within 48 hours of a complaint. When an owner does not comply voluntarily, the city lists these best-case timelines:

  • Weeds: 14 days, with vegetation over 12 inches prohibited.
  • Inoperable vehicles: 21 days, then towing.
  • Sanitation: 21 days, covering trash, tires, mattresses, appliances and similar items left outside.
  • Housing violations: 4 to 6 months.
  • Unsafe structures: 6 to 12 months.

If a violation is not fixed, the city can abate it and bill the owner for the work plus administrative and penalty fees. You can ask for an administrative hearing, which the city holds twice a month. About 30 to 40 structures are demolished each year, by the city or by the owner, so a badly deteriorated house can end up in that process.

Owners of properties vacant for more than 180 days must register them under Chapter 8.65 of the city code, adopted in November 2019. The Property Maintenance Unit sends a notice to owners it determines are vacant, and an owner who disagrees can file a dispute with the city.

This hits inherited houses and out-of-town owners most often. If you are holding an empty Topeka house while an estate settles, check whether you have received a registration notice and answer it. A sale usually goes faster when the city file is clean.

Short-term rentals in most residential zones need an administrative permit that lasts two years. Topeka has three types: Type I for owner-occupied homes, Type II for non-owner-occupied homes and Type III for homes with six or more guest bedrooms.

The city also bars landlords from retaliating against a tenant who complains in good faith about housing conditions. Under Topeka Municipal Code 9.25.020, evicting a tenant, raising rent or cutting services within six months of such a complaint is unlawful. Eviction for unpaid rent or lease violations is still allowed. If a tenant lives in the house you plan to sell, plan the timing around those limits.

sections.h2: Shawnee County valuation and tax dates
sections.html:
The Shawnee County Appraiser mails Change of Value Notices for real property on February 27. The county treasurer lists real estate tax as due in two halves.

DateEvent
February 27Change of Value Notices mailed for real property
March 30Deadline for informal real property value or classification appeal
May 1Real property informal conferences completed
May 10Second half real estate tax due
December 20First half real estate tax due

There are two routes to challenge a value. You can contact the county appraiser within 30 days of the notice mailing, or you can file a payment under protest form with the county treasurer when you pay. If a Topeka house sells in spring, the March appeal window and the May second-half payment can both fall inside the sale period.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Shawnee County
sections.html:
The Shawnee County Register of Deeds lists $21.00 for the first page of a deed, mortgage or other instrument. The fee schedule also adds $1.00 if signer or notary names are not plainly typed or printed under the signatures.

Kansas registers of deeds require a real estate sales validation questionnaire with a deed, or a clearly stated exemption on the deed, under K.S.A. 79-1437c and 79-1437e. The title company normally prepares that form. You can help by giving exact legal names and confirming how the owner or owners hold title.

sections.h2: What Topeka sellers usually deal with
sections.html:
The common cases are older houses needing work, inherited property, tenant situations and code violations that have been piling up. A cash buyer can take on those conditions where a conventional buyer's lender may not.

  • Older housing: homes from the railroad and early capital decades may carry deferred maintenance.
  • Code letters: a notice from the Property Maintenance Unit has response deadlines, so read it early.
  • Vacancy: a house empty for 180 days triggers a registration requirement.
  • Weather history: the city was struck by an F5 tornado on June 8, 1966, so roof and storm history is worth documenting.

Before you talk to any buyer, gather the latest Shawnee County tax statement, any city notice and the names exactly as they appear on the deed.

sections.h2: How a Topeka sale gets to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company or closing attorney checks the record for liens and unpaid taxes and prepares the deed. They also total what will be paid from your proceeds, including any mortgage payoff and the current tax bill. At closing you sign the deed, and the Register of Deeds records it.

If a code notice is open, the title company will want to know. Bring the notice and proof of any repair. Bring photo ID and all keys too. If the house is vacant, confirm the registration status with the city beforehand.

Start with your latest Shawnee County tax statement and your Change of Value Notice. Add any letter from the Property Maintenance Unit, proof of repairs, and the lease if a tenant lives there. Check how your name appears on the deed, because the closing paperwork has to match it. A short folder with these papers lets a buyer give you a firm number sooner.

sections.h2: What a cash sale leaves out
sections.html:
A listing usually means repairs, photos, showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval. A cash buyer skips those steps and closes when you choose. You still get a title search and a proper closing.

If the house is in good shape and you can wait, a listing may reach more buyers. Contact us with the address and we will give you a straight answer on which route looks better.

faqs.a: Shawnee County, and Topeka is the county seat. Values, tax bills and deeds are handled by county offices, while the city handles code enforcement and permits.

faqs.q: When are Shawnee County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due December 20 and the second half is due May 10.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Topeka home value?
faqs.a: The Shawnee County Appraiser sets March 30 as the deadline for an informal value or classification appeal, with informal conferences completed by May 1. An appeal starts within 30 days of the notice mailing date.

faqs.q: What happens if my Topeka house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The Property Maintenance Unit sends a notice and allows time to fix it. If the violation stays, the city can abate it and charge the owner the cost plus administrative and penalty fees, and you can request an administrative hearing.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a vacant house in Topeka?
faqs.a: Yes, if it has been vacant for more than 180 days. Chapter 8.65 of the city code requires registration, and the city mails notices to owners it believes are in that situation.
